If/when the revolver draws, a real draw would need to be modeled as an added funding entry (permanent, non-revolving in the engine's eyes) or the schedule would understate covenant-support cash interest/principal from that point on.

amortization_base.engine_limitation_note: ENGINE LIMITATION -- READ BEFORE RELYING ON THIS SCHEDULE'S scheduled_principal FIGURES. The agreement's own phrase ('0.60% of BEGINNING principal monthly') and the borrower's own certified monthly Debt & Liquidity schedules (every Monthly_Financial_Package reviewed, Jan 2025 - Jun 2026) both show a DECLINING-BALANCE mechanic: 0.60% is applied to that month's own opening balance, so the dollar amortization shrinks every month -- verified Jan 2025 $1,123,649.58 (= 0.60% x $187,274,929.89, ties by coincidence since month 1's opening balance equals original principal under either reading), Feb 2025 $1,116,907.68 (= 0.60% x $186,151,280.31, the DECLINED balance, not $187,274,929.89), Mar 2025 $1,110,206.24 (= 0.60% x $185,034,372.63). debt_service.py v1's amortization base is instead fixed at 'the aggregate original principal of all fundings dated strictly before the payment date' -- constant at $187,274,929.89 absent a new draw -- which produces a FLAT $1,123,649.58 installment every month rather than the true shrinking one. The two readings tie ONLY in month 1 (Jan 2025) and diverge every month after, with the gap widening: over the 18 certified months Jan 2025 - Jun 2026, the borrower's actual cumulative principal reduction is $187,274,929.89 - $168,048,469.80 (Q2 2026 certified Funded Debt) = $19,226,460.09, versus this engine's flat-base cumulative of 18 x $1,123,649.58 = $20,225,692.44 -- about $999,232 (5.2%) too high, and increasing every subsequent month. This is a v1 engine capability gap (no declining-balance base is supported), not a data-entry error.
amortization_base.open_question: Because the agreement's ENTIRE amortization provision is this one sentence -- no separate 'base' definition, no worked example, no schedule -- 'beginning principal' is also textually capable of meaning the ORIGINAL principal at inception (which the engine models) rather than each month's own opening balance (which the borrower's books actually use). Given 18 straight months of the borrower's own contemporaneous, internally-tying accounting apply the declining-balance reading, that is the reading recorded as governing the facts; the flat reading is what this generated schedule can mechanically produce. Recommendation for step 7: DO NOT rely on this generated schedule's scheduled_principal / month_end_balance / balloon figures for Veyrona -- read the borrower's own certified Debt & Liquidity tab (Beginning Debt / Scheduled Principal / Ending Debt) for actual monthly principal and outstanding balance, exactly as is already done for a sibling facility in this portfolio with the identical clause and the identical engine gap.

margin_grid.when: PLACEHOLDER ONLY -- NOT A CONTRACTUAL RATE. No index, margin, floor, or fixed cash-pay rate is stated anywhere in the Original Credit Agreement, the First/Second/Third Amendments, the Guaranty, the Security Agreement, or the Closing Certificate. Confirmed by a full-text sweep of every executed document for 'interest', 'rate', 'LIBOR', 'SOFR', 'Prime', 'margin', 'index', 'PIK', 'per annum', and 'basis point' -- zero matches outside this note. No Fee Letter or pricing-side-letter exists anywhere in the deal folder to reconcile against (unlike a sibling facility in this portfolio, where an actual Fee Letter exists). The borrower's own monthly financial packages carry NO interest-expense line at all (the Income Statement stops at Revenue / Cost of Revenue / Operating Expenses / Reported EBITDA) and no Debt & Liquidity column for interest either -- so there is also no certified figure to reverse-engineer a rate from. This 1-basis-point rate exists ONLY because the engine refuses a rate of exactly zero on a fixed-rate (index: null) facility ('would mean an interest-free loan'); it is not a market estimate and should not be read as one. EVERY cash_interest_accrued / cash_paid_total figure in the generated schedule is therefore void pending confirmation of actual pricing with Granite Harbor Direct Lending, LP -- this is a genuine, prominent drafting gap, not an extraction miss.
